# Print issues: the four gaps left by hiding OrcaSlicer's notices

Dates: 2026-10-09 and 10. Untracked on purpose; nothing here is committed and no fix is shipped.

JusPrin hides every OrcaSlicer pop-up notice while its shell is installed and shows print problems in its own list instead. This report covers the four costs of that decision: operation notices with no replacement, one uncovered warning, future upstream warnings, and readers that had never been triggered. One small addition to OrcaSlicer's notification manager (9 lines, measured to merge cleanly) answers three of the four. Running the readers for the first time found three defects and one check that can never fire.

## Where this was done

- Worktree `.claude/worktrees/blissful-dhawan-1561d5`, at `jusprin-newui` commit `570e3fb1c7`, with the uncommitted feature copied in from `wonderful-roentgen-83d009` on 2026-10-09 12:47. That worktree's monitor and notification manager lines were unchanged when I re-checked on 2026-10-10; other files there had moved on.
- My additions, all prototype: a read accessor on `NotificationManager` (2 files), a variant of the two-line draw suppression (same file), and a new harness mode `--print-issue-readers` in `tests/shell/print_issue_readers_scenario.inc` (20 steps, group chosen with the `JUSPRIN_READER_STEPS` environment variable).
- Evidence: run logs, the kind inventory and the guard demonstration are in `investigation-print-issues-four-gaps/`.
- Merge simulations: fork base `3ffb9585d2`, upstream `b3490a1cdc` (2026-10-09), command `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=3ffb9585d2 upstream/main <commit>`. Baseline `570e3fb1c7` has 3,889 conflicted files. The feature as copied (commit object `7381ccdd44`, on no branch) has the same list.

| Candidate upstream edit | Commit object | Lines | Conflicted files | Same list as baseline | Upstream commits at the site since fork base / in 2 years |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Read accessor `for_each_notification` | `cdab601150` | +9 in 2 files | 3,889 | Yes | 0 / 0 |
| Flushing check made public | `2700b20710` | +2 in 1 file | 3,889 | Yes | 0 / 1 (declaration); 1 / 4 (body) |
| Push hook carrying kind and level | `e2abf87fab` | +1 −2, fork's own lines | 3,889 | Yes | 0 / 0 (those lines); 2 / 3 (function) |
| Draw suppression that keeps the end of the function running | `528b14d297` | +3 instead of +2 | 3,889 | Yes | 1 / 3 (function) |

In all four the natural resolution is correct: nothing upstream is deleted or rewritten, and the merged text was read back.

## Problem 1: operation notices have no replacement

**Recommendation.** Mirror, do not record. Add one read accessor to the notification manager and let a fork-owned table decide, per kind, where a held notice appears. The premise that these are "events with nothing to re-ask" is only partly true: OrcaSlicer keeps every notice for at least 5 seconds, most for 10 to 20, and many until it closes them itself. With drawing off nobody can dismiss one, so the manager is a reliable store for as long as the notice lives.

**Evidence.**

- Inventory of all 62 kinds in `notice-inventory.md`: 21 are print problems, 27 are operation or application notices that are now shown nowhere, 14 are unused or not worth showing. Worst today: the header's "Export sliced file…" ends with no confirmation; a refused arrange ("This plate is locked") looks like nothing happened; background job progress and its Cancel are invisible; a preset sync conflict cannot be resolved because its two buttons are never drawn.
- Runtime: an export-finished notice pushed while the shell is installed was held by the manager, drawn 0 times, absent from the issue list, and read back through the accessor with its text (`run_e.log`).
- The existing hook (`report_file_load_message` in `push_notification_data`) can carry kind and level by changing the fork's own three lines to two, and that merges cleanly. I do not recommend relying on it. It runs before the notice is stored, and it never sees progress updates, closes, the action behind a link, or the ten `bbl_show_*` functions that update a notice in place. OrcaSlicer already schedules a canvas frame on every push, so the overlay can read the manager each frame with no hook at all.
- Actions are the hard part. A link's callback lives inside a private object. Open folder and Eject can be done by fork code through public functions. Upload progress and cancel are better read from the upload queue's own public events than from the notice.

**Decisions for Kenneth.**

1. Which groups matter first. My order: results of an action (export finished, arrange refused, repair finished), then long-running work, then application state.
2. Where they appear: a short-lived confirmation in the canvas corner above the issue pill, progress in the header beside slicing, application state on Home.
3. Whether the tips and the object size card are dropped.
4. Whether a stopgap is wanted: let OrcaSlicer draw a chosen few kinds natively. It costs about three upstream lines and keeps every native button, in the native look. It reverses part of "hide all".

## Problem 2: "flushing volume set to 0" is not covered

**Recommendation.** Read it from the notification manager through the same accessor. If the accessor is rejected, make the check public instead. Do not copy the check.

**Evidence.**

- Reproduced the gap: with every flushing value zero on a two-filament plate, OrcaSlicer held its warning and the monitor reported nothing. Slicing was still allowed (`run_c.log`, step `c5`).
- Upstream rewrote this check on 2026-08-13 (commit `78eef79ffe`): it now ignores single-filament plates and unused filaments. A copy made at the fork base would already be wrong.
- Reading the notice costs no further upstream lines once the accessor exists, uses OrcaSlicer's own sentence, and is exactly as fresh as the stock notice. The kind has a single producer, so there is nothing to tell apart.
- Making the check public is 2 added lines and merges cleanly, but the fork then repeats the sentence as a translation key, which drifts silently if upstream rewords it.
- There is no other public route today. After the next rebase upstream has a public helper for the zero test, but the conditions for when it applies stay in the private function.

**Decision.** Accessor or public function.

## Problem 3: new upstream warnings will be invisible

**Recommendation.** Three layers, because each catches what the others miss.

1. **Build time.** A fork-owned `switch` over `NotificationType` with no default, and the missing-case warning turned into an error for that file. A new kind stops the build until someone classifies it.
2. **Test time.** A test that reads the canvas warning list from `GLCanvas3D.hpp` and counts callers of the push functions, compared with a list the fork owns. The canvas enum is private, so fork code cannot name it; a text scan is the only way without an upstream edit.
3. **Run time.** A catch-all reader over warning and error level notices that no specific reader explains, shown as plate-wide issues in OrcaSlicer's words.

**Evidence.**

- Since the fork base upstream added 6 kinds, 1 canvas warning and 23 new call sites that push a notice. Two of the new kinds are print problems that would be invisible after the next rebase: single-extruder mixed filament risk, and mixed filament broken.
- Layer 1 demonstrated standalone (`kind-guard-demo.cpp`): it compiles against the fork's enum and fails against upstream's with "6 enumeration values not handled in switch", naming them.
- 19 of the 23 new call sites are plain `push_notification` calls that add no enum value. Only layers 2 and 3 see those.
- The two shared kinds, slicing error and plate error, each hold one notice at a time, because a second push replaces the text of the first. The catch-all can therefore decide by presence: if a specific reader already produced an issue of that kind, the notice is explained; if not, show it. No text is compared.
- The catch-all is only trustworthy with the draw-suppression variant under "Defects found". Without it, a plate warning closed by opening a project is never deleted and OrcaSlicer refuses to push the same words again.

**Decisions.** Accept a build that stops when upstream adds a kind. Accept raw OrcaSlicer text for unexplained notices.

## Problem 4: the readers had never been triggered

Run in the real application through the harness, on Bambu Lab X1 Carbon (0.4 and 0.6 nozzle) and H2D (two nozzles). "Same words" means the monitor's text equals OrcaSlicer's own notice text after its "Error:" or "Warning:" first line, compared in the same run.

| Condition | Recipe | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Two or more TPU filaments | H2D, two TPU filaments, both in use | **Cannot fire.** `PartPlate::check_tpu_printable_status` returns true unconditionally in this version. OrcaSlicer let it slice |
| Filament not printable | H2D, TPU 95A HF mapped by hand to the left nozzle | Reproduced. Blocker, OrcaSlicer refuses to slice, same words |
| PLA with PETG | X1 Carbon 0.4, PLA Basic and PETG Basic, one object each | Reproduced. Warning, same words. On H2D OrcaSlicer does not warn (its profile has a tool change time of 5.6, which OrcaSlicer's rule treats as separate nozzles) and neither does the monitor |
| Nozzle and filament incompatible | X1 Carbon 0.6 nozzle, PLA Silk | Reproduced. Warning, same words |
| Filament mixture incompatible | H2D, PVA and PETG Basic | Reproduced. Warning, same words |
| Prime tower outside the plate | H2D, two filaments, tower placed 8 mm from the right edge, sliced | Reproduced. Warning, same words |
| A filament its nozzle cannot reach | H2D, filament 2 mapped to the right nozzle, its cube 12 mm from the left edge; also a 322 mm column on the left nozzle | Reproduced both. Blocker, same words. **The issue has no object target** although OrcaSlicer's sentence names the model |
| Toolpath outside the plate | X1 Carbon, cube 1 mm inside the right edge, 3 skirt loops at 6 mm | Reproduced. Blocker, OrcaSlicer refuses to print, same words. A brim does not work: OrcaSlicer trims it at the edge |
| Nozzle printable area after slicing | The prime tower slice above | Reproduced. Blocker. **Words differ**: OrcaSlicer says "Filaments 1, 1 are placed…", the monitor says "Filaments 1 are placed…" |
| Filament not printable on the plate surface | X1 Carbon, first-layer bed temperature set to 0 in the filament settings, sliced | Reproduced. Blocker, OrcaSlicer refuses to print |
| Slicing failure that names its object | A 20 mm body resting on a 0.1 mm point, no supports | Reproduced. The failure carries the object OrcaSlicer named |
| G-code processor warnings | Any H2D slice here | Reproduced: the "heatbed temperature is relatively high" warning. I found no place where stock OrcaSlicer shows this one before the send dialog, so the monitor shows more than stock here |
| Toolpath above the print height | A column 2 mm taller than the printer | **Unverified.** OrcaSlicer blocks it before slicing as an object outside the plate, which the monitor reports. I found no way to produce the post-slice case |
| Nozzle printable height after slicing | The 322 mm column on the left nozzle | **Unverified** for the same reason. Reading the code, OrcaSlicer's notice also ends with "Open wiki for more information." and the monitor's does not |

## Defects found

1. **The monitor calls a path "blocking" when OrcaSlicer still prints it.** A skirt 1.2 mm past the plate edge: the monitor reported a blocker; OrcaSlicer's own ready-to-print test passed and the header's Print was enabled (`run_c.log`, step `a5`). The reader runs its own geometry test, while OrcaSlicer refuses on its stored post-slice check, which allows 2 mm. Proposed: take "blocks" from that stored result, which also covers two of its values the monitor does not read today.
2. **The two-line draw suppression changes how notices live.** The end of `render_notifications` deletes a closed plate warning and records the time of the last draw; the early return skips both. Reproduced: a plate warning closed the way opening a project closes it is drawn again in the stock presentation (1 of 1), and never again once drawing had been suppressed (0 of 1). A variant that skips only the drawing loop restores it (1 of 1), still draws nothing while the shell is installed, and merges cleanly. Not run against the 42-step print-issues scenario. The stale draw time also makes delayed notices fire at once; that part is from reading the code.
3. **Nozzle-reach issues carry no object.**
4. **Nozzle-area words differ from OrcaSlicer's.**

## Not done

- No monitor change. The catch-all reader and the flushing reader are designs backed by the accessor's runtime output, not code.
- Layer 2 of the guard is described and measured, not written as a test.
- Windows and Linux.
- The duplicated timelapse warning: reading the code, OrcaSlicer stores two processor warnings with the same words and different codes, which the monitor would list twice. Not reproduced.


content.text:
JusPrin hides every OrcaSlicer pop-up notice and shows print problems in its own list; I investigated the four gaps that leaves. One 9-line read accessor on OrcaSlicer's notification manager answers three of them, and running the new readers for the first time found four defects in the candidate. Nothing is committed or shipped.

## Problem 1: operation notices have no replacement
- **Recommendation:** read notices back from the notification manager through the accessor, and let a fork-owned table decide per kind where each appears. OrcaSlicer keeps a notice for seconds at least, and nobody can dismiss one while drawing is off.
- **Evidence:** of 62 kinds, 21 are print problems and 27 are operation or application notices now shown nowhere. An export-finished notice was held by the manager, drawn 0 times, and read back with its text.
- **Existing hook:** it can carry kind and level with no extra upstream lines, but it never sees progress, closes or link actions, so I would not rely on it.

## Problem 2: "flushing volume set to 0"
- **Recommendation:** read it through the same accessor; if you reject the accessor, make the check public (2 added lines).
- **Evidence:** I reproduced the gap. Upstream rewrote this check on 2026-08-13, so a copy made at the fork base would already be wrong.

## Problem 3: future upstream warnings
- **Recommendation:** three layers.
  - A `switch` over the notice kinds that stops the build when upstream adds one.
  - A test that scans the canvas warning list and counts the places that push a notice.
  - A catch-all that shows any warning or error notice no reader explains.
- **Evidence:** since the fork base upstream added 6 kinds, 1 canvas warning and 23 new places that push a notice. The switch compiled against the fork's kinds and failed against upstream's, naming the new ones (demonstrated standalone).

## Problem 4: readers never triggered
- **Reproduced (11 of 14):** all but the three below, on the X1 Carbon and the two-nozzle H2D.
- **Cannot fire (1):** OrcaSlicer's "two or more TPU filaments" check always passes in this version.
- **Unverified (2):** path above the print height, and nozzle height after slicing. OrcaSlicer blocks a too-tall object before slicing.
- **Wording:** seven notices matched OrcaSlicer's words exactly. The nozzle-area sentence differs: OrcaSlicer says "Filaments 1, 1", the monitor says "Filaments 1".

## Defects found in the candidate
1. A skirt 1.2 mm past the plate edge is listed as blocking while OrcaSlicer still allows Print.
2. The two-line draw suppression skips the end of the function. A plate warning closed by opening a project is never deleted, and OrcaSlicer then refuses to show the same warning again, even after switching back to the classic view. A 3-line variant fixed this in my run; I did not run it against the full print-issues scenario.
3. "Nozzle cannot reach" issues carry no object, although OrcaSlicer's sentence names the model.
4. The nozzle-area wording difference above.

## Upstream footprint
All four candidate edits were simulated against upstream `b3490a1cdc` from fork base `3ffb9585d2`. Each leaves the list of 3,889 conflicted files identical to the baseline.

| Edit | Lines | Commit object |
|---|---|---|
| Read accessor | +9 in 2 files | `cdab601150` |
| Flushing check made public | +2 | `2700b20710` |
| Hook carrying kind and level | +1 −2 | `e2abf87fab` |
| Draw suppression variant | +3 instead of +2 | `528b14d297` |

## Decisions for you
1. Accept the accessor, or make the flushing check public instead?
2. Accept a build that stops whenever upstream adds a notice kind?
3. May unexplained notices appear in the issue list in OrcaSlicer's raw words?
4. Which operation notices come first, and where do they go? I suggest action results in the canvas corner, progress in the header, and application state on Home.
5. Should the four defects be fixed in the candidate before it is committed?

The work is in worktree `.claude/worktrees/blissful-dhawan-1561d5`, untracked: the report is `investigation-print-issues-four-gaps.md`, with run logs and the kind inventory in the folder of the same name. The new harness mode is `--print-issue-readers`.

Keep print issues on the Prepare canvas, with Ask AI and Resolve with AI

A print problem was only visible as an OrcaSlicer notice in the corner of
the 3D view, or somewhere back in the chat. Inside the JusPrin shell those
notices are now replaced by a status in the canvas's lower right corner, the
list it opens, and a bubble beside the object the selected issue is about.
The bubble's two buttons send the issue to the project chat.

The list (PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor) holds no rule about what a problem
is. It asks OrcaSlicer's own checks again and reads the state OrcaSlicer
already stores: Print::validate, a copy over the plate's edge, the plate's
filament and nozzle checks, slicing step warnings, the slice result, and why
the last slice failed. An issue exists while its native source reports it.
While OrcaSlicer holds an edit it has not yet applied to the print, the
issues are marked stale, the status says it is checking, and the buttons
are off, so "no print issues" is never shown before a check. Only the
active plate is reported, because that is the only plate OrcaSlicer checks.

Canvas (PrintIssues/IssueOverlay, IssueOverlayLayout): drawn with ImGui
through the overlay hook the tool strip uses. The bubble goes above its
object, else right, left or below, and never covers the object, the status,
the open list or the tool strip. It docks beside the status for a
plate-wide issue or an object out of view. Every finding on one object
shares the bubble through a pager. Selecting an issue selects its copy by
OrcaSlicer's own id, so two objects with one name cannot be confused.

Chat (AgentHost::submit_issue_message, PrintIssues/IssueContext): a press
becomes an ordinary user message, the request sentence with OrcaSlicer's
words quoted beneath it, and carries the issue, its target and the
freshness of the evidence as data for the model. It shares the page's own
message path, obeys the same refusals, and leaves the composer's draft
alone. The issue is looked up again at the press, so one that has cleared
or gone stale is not sent. Ask AI may only read: the turn is offered the
read-only tools and the host refuses a call to any other. Resolve with AI
is an ordinary turn. With no assistant set up, a press sends nothing and
offers to open the chat panel's setup.

OrcaSlicer-owned files: two added lines in
NotificationManager::render_notifications return early while the Prepare
canvas has its legacy overlays hidden, the flag the shell already sets on
install and restores when switching to the classic presentation. Only the
drawing stops; notices are still pushed, timed out and closed. The Prepare
canvas is asked, not the canvas being drawn, because Check print is a
second canvas without the flag and drew the notices again. The reason a
slice failed is read from EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED, which Plater.cpp defines
and no header declared; it is declared in a fork header Plater.cpp already
includes, with no OrcaSlicer line changed.

Rebase evidence (fork base 3ffb9585d2, upstream/main b3490a1cdc): the
conflict list from git merge-tree is the same with and without this change.
The two lines sit after sort_notifications() because upstream has since
added a line at the top of that function, which they would otherwise have
collided with. No upstream line is deleted or rewritten.

Known limits, recorded in agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md: notices that
are not print problems (export finished, upload and download progress,
update and network notices) have no JusPrin surface yet and are no longer
seen; the "flushing volume set to 0" warning is not read, because its check
is private to GLCanvas3D; a warning kind upstream adds later needs a reader
before it is shown. The plate-check and post-slice readers were not

The print-issues feature is now committed on `jusprin-newui` as `6394191523`, so I moved my worktree onto that commit and redid the whole investigation there. Every finding holds, and none of the four gaps is fixed by the commit: its own "Known limits" paragraph names the same four.

## What I did
- **Worktree:** fast-forwarded `.claude/worktrees/blissful-dhawan-1561d5` to `6394191523`, dropped my old copy of the feature, and re-applied only my prototype on top (nothing staged, nothing committed).
- **Prototype:** now one file, `investigation-print-issues-four-gaps/prototype.patch`. It holds the 9-line read accessor, the 3-line variant of the draw suppression, and the `--print-issue-readers` harness mode.
- **Same code:** the commit's print-issue monitor and its two notification manager lines are identical to the copy I first measured.

## Re-run on the commit
- **Reproductions:** same results as before. Eleven of fourteen conditions reproduce, the "two or more TPU filaments" check still cannot fire, and two post-slice height cases stay unverified.
- **Defects:** all four reproduce on the committed code.
  - A skirt 1.2 mm past the plate edge is listed as blocking while Print stays enabled.
  - A plate warning closed while drawing is suppressed is never shown again (0 of 1, against 1 of 1 in the control).
  - "Nozzle cannot reach" issues carry no object.
  - The nozzle-area sentence differs from OrcaSlicer's.
- **Variant check that was missing before:** the commit's own 42-step print-issues scenario passes with my draw-suppression variant, with 0 failed checks and 0 notices drawn in all 85 samples and in Check print.

## Merge simulations, redone with the commit as baseline
The baseline `6394191523` has 3,889 conflicted files against upstream `b3490a1cdc` (fork base `3ffb9585d2`). Each candidate leaves that list identical.

| Edit | Lines | New commit object |
|---|---|---|
| Read accessor | +9 in 2 files | `c5ef7a8157` |
| Flushing check made public | +2 | `059bd32816` |
| Hook carrying kind and level | +1 −2 | `be0a9f45ff` |
| Draw suppression variant | +3 −2 | `8bd274cc02` |

## Still yours to decide
The five decisions from my last message are unchanged. The one that is now more pressing is whether to fix the four defects, since they are in committed code rather than a candidate.

The report is updated in place at `investigation-print-issues-four-gaps.md` in my worktree, and the evidence logs in the folder of the same name were replaced with the runs made on the commit.

Explain to me what the problems are in plain English.  Then, explain what decisions you needed from me in Plain English.  Actually, you need to give me some fucking idea about what all this is all about, because this is a task that some other agent threw over the world to me.

## What this is about

OrcaSlicer shows small pop-up messages in the lower right corner of the 3D view. They cover everything from "your object hangs off the plate" to "export finished" to "an update is available".

You decided JusPrin should replace those pop-ups with its own design: a small status pill in that corner, a list of what is wrong with the print, and a bubble next to the affected object with "Ask AI" and "Resolve with AI". That feature was built by another session and you committed it yesterday.

To make it work, JusPrin switches off drawing of **all** OrcaSlicer pop-ups, then rebuilds the print-problem ones itself by asking OrcaSlicer directly what is wrong. Switching off all of them had four known side effects. The agent that built the feature wrote them down and handed them to me. My job was to investigate each one and propose a fix, without shipping anything.

## The four problems

1. **Messages that are not print problems vanished too.** Example: you click "Export sliced file" in the JusPrin header and nothing tells you it worked. The same goes for "this plate is locked, can't arrange", upload progress, update available, and about 25 other kinds.

2. **One real print warning is missing.** "Flushing volume set to 0, colours may mix" is not in the new list. OrcaSlicer keeps that check private, so JusPrin cannot ask it.

3. **Future OrcaSlicer warnings will be silently invisible.** When OrcaSlicer adds a new warning, JusPrin shows nothing for it and nobody is told. This already applies: OrcaSlicer has added two new print warnings since the fork point (June) that would be invisible after the next update.

4. **Most of the new code had never actually been run.** The test setup had a simple one-nozzle printer, so warnings about two nozzles, mixed materials and similar had never been triggered.

## What I found

**For problems 1, 2 and 3, one small change covers all three.** OrcaSlicer still keeps every message internally; JusPrin just doesn't draw them. If JusPrin can read that internal list (9 added lines in one OrcaSlicer file, and I checked it merges cleanly with current OrcaSlicer), it can:
- show "export finished" and similar in its own style
- pick up the flushing warning
- show any warning it doesn't recognise as a plain entry in the list.

**For problem 4, I ran them.** Eleven of fourteen work correctly. One can never trigger because OrcaSlicer itself disabled that check. Two I could not trigger.

**Running them exposed four bugs in the committed feature:**
- JusPrin says "this blocks printing" for a path slightly past the plate edge, while the Print button is still enabled. OrcaSlicer allows 2 mm; JusPrin allows none.
- If someone switches back to the classic OrcaSlicer look, some warnings never appear again for the rest of the session. I have a 3-line fix that passed the feature's full test run.
- The "nozzle can't reach this object" problem doesn't point at the object, so no bubble appears next to it.
- One sentence reads slightly differently from OrcaSlicer's ("Filaments 1" versus "Filaments 1, 1").

## What I need from you

1. **May I add those 9 lines to an OrcaSlicer file?** Every line added there has to be carried through each OrcaSlicer update. If no, the fallback fixes only the flushing warning (2 lines) and leaves problems 1 and 3 open.

2. **Should the build fail when OrcaSlicer adds a new message type?** That forces someone to decide what JusPrin does with it. The cost is one extra chore at each OrcaSlicer update.

3. **Is it acceptable to show an unrecognised warning in OrcaSlicer's raw wording?** The alternative is showing nothing.

4. **Which missing messages do you want back first, and where?** My suggestion: results of an action (export finished, arrange refused) as a brief confirmation in the canvas corner; progress in the header; update and account messages on Home.

5. **Should I fix the four bugs now?** They are in committed code. I'd say yes to all four.

Nothing is committed. The full write-up is `investigation-print-issues-four-gaps.md` in my worktree.

You told me what the problem was and the new bugs. And then you skipped telling me about what you were proposing and asking me if I should accept your proposal. How should I respond? Should I just blindly say yes because you're God?

No. Here is what each proposal actually is, what it costs, where it is weak, and what the alternative is.

## Proposal 1: let JusPrin read OrcaSlicer's message list

**What it is.** OrcaSlicer still keeps every pop-up message in memory; JusPrin just doesn't draw them. I add one small read-only function to OrcaSlicer's code so JusPrin can read each message's kind, how serious it is, and its text.

**What you get.** JusPrin can then show the flushing warning, show "export finished" and similar in its own style, and notice warnings nobody wrote special handling for.

**Cost.** Nine lines in an OrcaSlicer file, carried through every OrcaSlicer update. That spot has not changed upstream in two years.

**Weak points.**
- Only the reading is proven. The JusPrin side that displays these messages is not built or designed.
- Buttons on messages (Open folder, Eject, Cancel upload) do not come through. JusPrin would rebuild each one it wants.
- It is only reliable together with bug fix 2 below.
- The agent that built the feature rejected reading this list for print problems, because it loses which object a message is about. I agree. I propose it only for things with no better source.

**Alternatives.**
- Flushing warning only: expose that one check (2 lines). Leaves problems 1 and 3 open.
- Let OrcaSlicer draw its own pop-ups again for non-print messages (about 3 lines). Cheapest, and all buttons work, but it looks like OrcaSlicer and partly undoes your "hide all" decision.

**My recommendation.** Yes, if you want JusPrin-styled messages. If you want export confirmation back this week with no design work, take the second alternative as a stopgap.

## Proposal 2: fail the build when OrcaSlicer adds a message kind

**What it is.** A list in JusPrin's code naming all 62 message kinds and what JusPrin does with each. If OrcaSlicer adds a kind that is not on the list, the build stops and names it.

**Cost.** One line per new kind at each update; six since June.

**Weak point.** It misses new warnings that reuse an existing kind, which is most of them: 19 of the 23 added since June.

**Alternative.** The note in the docs that exists today, which relies on someone remembering.

**My recommendation.** Yes. It is cheap and nothing else here forces a person to look.

## Proposal 3: show unrecognised warnings in OrcaSlicer's raw words

**What it is.** A warning that JusPrin has no special handling for appears in the issue list as a "whole plate" entry with OrcaSlicer's text. This covers what proposal 2 misses.

**Weak points.**
- A message that is not about the print could land in the print issue list.
- Wrong duplicates or omissions are possible in edge cases.
- Not built.

**Alternative.** Show nothing, as today.

**My recommendation.** Yes, but only after I build it and show you real cases.

## Proposal 4: which missing messages come back, and where

This is a product call, not a technical one. I suggest starting with results of an action (export finished, arrange refused), shown briefly in the canvas corner. Nothing is designed.

## Proposal 5: the four bugs

1. **"Blocks printing" shown while Print is enabled.** I'd take the label from OrcaSlicer's own answer to "can this print". Alternative: leave it stricter than OrcaSlicer. I recommend fixing it, because the label contradicts the button.
2. **Warnings stuck hidden after switching to classic view.** Three lines instead of the current two in the OrcaSlicer file. Tested: the feature's 42-step run passes. I recommend fixing it.
3. **"Nozzle can't reach" has no object.** I have not tried the fix yet, so I can't promise it is small.
4. **"Filaments 1" versus "Filaments 1, 1".** OrcaSlicer's version looks like its own bug. I recommend leaving ours.

## How to answer

A safe answer that commits to little: yes to proposal 2 and to bug fixes 1 and 2. Then ask me to build proposals 1 and 3 as a prototype you can look at before deciding, and decide proposal 4 once you've seen it.

Mostly, yes. The read function is the same thing I proposed. The difference is how JusPrin finds out the list changed.

**What I proposed:** no second line in OrcaSlicer's code. JusPrin re-reads the list each time it draws its own overlay on the 3D view. The weakness is that a message that comes and goes while that view isn't being drawn (for example, while Home is showing) is missed.

**What the other agent proposes:** one extra line in OrcaSlicer's code that calls JusPrin from the function where OrcaSlicer itself ages and removes messages. JusPrin then compares the list with what it saw last time. I think this is the better trigger, because it does not depend on JusPrin's overlay being drawn. The cost is one more line to carry through OrcaSlicer updates, in a function upstream has not touched in two years.

Two things in that agent's sentence are wrong, and one of them matters:

- **It does not run every rendered frame.** OrcaSlicer calls that function whenever the 3D view is idle, not when it draws. This does not change the design.
- **It does not run at all while JusPrin is not the active window.** The function exits at its first lines in that case, so a call placed at the end is never reached. If someone starts an export and switches to another app, JusPrin hears about "export finished" only when they come back.

  Nothing should be lost, because OrcaSlicer also stops expiring messages while inactive. That is my reading of the code, not something I ran.

One limit applies to both versions: a message that is pushed and closed again within a moment (such as "Arranging…") can disappear before anyone reads it. That is fine for confirmations and wrong for progress, which should come from the job itself.

I have not checked that the extra line merges cleanly with current OrcaSlicer; I only did that for the read function. It is a few minutes' work if you want it.

Since the feature is off `jusprin-newui` for a redesign, treat this as input to that redesign, not something already agreed.

Okay, I think we have our final design. Let me rephrase it to make sure we are on the same page. 

1. The five signal firing triggers that in the current code need to be removed. 
2. We use the trigger we just talked about to intercept all the m changes in Notification manager. 
3. add Nine lines in an OrcaSlicer file to Read orcaslicer Message List  
4. We used the returned message list as a source of truth for drawing our own notification. 
5. Optionally we can use existing mechanism to retrieve the object attached to the message and highlight the object the same way as the current code.

content.text:
Points 2 and 3 match what I understand. Points 1, 4 and 5 each have one thing you should know before calling the design final. The first is a real hole I already have evidence for.

## Point 4 has a gap: some blockers are not in the list when you need them

Three problems only get a message from OrcaSlicer when the sliced preview is loaded, which in JusPrin means opening Check print:

- a path that goes outside the plate
- a filament its nozzle cannot reach (found after slicing)
- a filament that cannot print on this plate surface.

In my runs, right after slicing, OrcaSlicer's list held none of these. Print was already disabled, so the person would see a dead Print button with no reason given. The first two appeared in the list only after Check print was opened; I did not open Check print for the third, so that one is from reading the code.

Stock OrcaSlicer does not have this hole because it jumps to the preview after every slice. JusPrin stays on Prepare.

Three ways to close it:
- **Keep the small piece of current code that reads these three from the slice result.** This is my recommendation: it is already written and I ran it.
- **Load the preview quietly after each slice.** I have not tried this.
- **Accept that the reason only shows after Check print.** I would not.

## Point 5 is not free, and not really optional

The list gives the message's kind, seriousness and words. It does not give the object. OrcaSlicer tucks the object away inside each pop-up's "Jump to" link, where JusPrin cannot reach it.

So "retrieve the object" means keeping the current per-problem lookups and running them when a message of that kind shows up. That works for most kinds. Two consequences:

- **Point 1 becomes "remove four, keep one".** The object behind a failed slice only exists in the "slice finished" signal, so that one has to stay, as a data capture rather than a redraw trigger.
- **Without point 5 there is no bubble beside the object and no highlight.** If those stay in the product, point 5 is required.

## Two smaller things point 4 changes

- **"Checking…" goes away unless we keep it.** For about half a second after an edit, OrcaSlicer's list still describes the old state. The current code shows "Checking…" in that window and never says "no issues" too early. That needs one state read, no trigger.
- **Telling two messages of the same kind apart.** For a few kinds OrcaSlicer allows several at once, and the only difference the list exposes is the text. The handoff said never to identify by text. Either that rule relaxes for these kinds, or the nine lines grow a little.

## Two things the design depends on

- **The three-line change to how drawing is switched off.** Without it, some warnings get stuck and never re-enter the list. I reproduced that and tested the change.
- **A table saying what JusPrin does with each of the 62 kinds.** Point 4 cannot draw anything without it.

## What I need from you

1. Which way to close the gap after slicing?
2. Do the bubble and highlight stay? If yes, point 5 is in and point 1 is "remove four".
Keep the slice result readers, and keep the bubble and highlight

content.text:
Both decisions are recorded. Here is the design as it now stands, so we can confirm we mean the same thing.

## The agreed design

1. **OrcaSlicer's message list is the source of truth** for what JusPrin draws, for all messages, not only print problems.
2. **Nine lines in an OrcaSlicer file** let JusPrin read that list.
3. **One more line in the same file** tells JusPrin "the list may have changed, look again".
4. **Four of the five current triggers are removed.** The "slice finished" one stays, because it is the only place the object behind a failed slice exists.
5. **The slice-result readers stay.** They cover the three blockers that are missing from the list until Check print is opened.
6. **The bubble and highlight stay.** The current per-problem lookups remain and run when a message of that kind appears, to find its object.

## Cost in OrcaSlicer's code

All of it sits in the two notification manager files: 13 lines added and the feature's current 2 lines replaced. That includes the three-line change to how drawing is switched off, which this design depends on.

I checked the whole set against OrcaSlicer as of today, on top of the feature commit `6394191523`: it merges with no new conflicts. To do that I fetched the latest OrcaSlicer, so the baseline count other reports quote (3,889 conflicted files) is now 3,892.

## What I assumed, since you did not say otherwise

- **"Checking…" stays**, so JusPrin never says "no issues" in the half second before OrcaSlicer has caught up.
- **A table lists what JusPrin does with each of the 62 message kinds.** Nothing can be drawn without it. The build stops if OrcaSlicer adds a kind that is not in the table.

## Still open

1. **Telling apart two messages of the same kind.** The only difference OrcaSlicer exposes is the text. Either the "never identify by text" rule relaxes for those few kinds, or the nine lines grow by a couple. I'd relax the rule for those kinds only.
2. **Who builds this, and where.** Another agent is clearly working on the same design. I have not started, so that two sessions do not write the same code. If you want me to build it, I'd branch from `feature-popup-message-handling`, where the feature commit lives, unless you say otherwise.

> Telling apart two messages of the same kind. The only difference OrcaSlicer exposes is the text. Either the “never identify by text” rule relaxes for those few kinds, or the nine lines grow by a couple. I’d relax the rule for those kinds only.

Go back to the original source for the never identified by text rule. If the rule was there to make sure that we don't hard code some text message because it's a brittle Design, then it's irrelevant here because we're comparing real-time variable with another real-time variable that should be identical to begin with, right? If the original source had some other good reason why we shouldn't compare text, then stop. Otherwise proceed.

> Who builds this, and where.

No other agent is working on it.

python3 - <<'EOF'
r='/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/blissful-dhawan-1561d5/agent-docs/jusprin/'
p=r+'architecture.md'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
a=s[s.index("### Print issues\n"):s.index("### Agent WebView\n")]
b='''### Print issues and OrcaSlicer's notifications

Inside the shell OrcaSlicer's own notifications are held but not drawn. JusPrin reads the list back and draws what it holds: print problems as a status pill in the canvas's lower right corner, the list it opens, and a bubble beside the object the selected issue is about, with **Ask AI** and **Resolve with AI**; the outcome of an action (export finished, an arrange that was refused) as a short confirmation above the pill.

**OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth.** A notification carries a kind, a level and words. It does not carry the object it is about, so where OrcaSlicer lets its check be asked again, that check is asked once more for the object only.

| Piece | Owns |
|---|---|
| `PrintIssues/NoticeKinds` | Where each of OrcaSlicer's notification kinds goes: the issue list, a confirmation, running work, application state, or nowhere. Every kind is named; a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in this file until someone routes it. |
| `PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor` | Reads the list on the notification manager's own turn, compares it with what it saw last, and rebuilds only on a change. Asks OrcaSlicer's checks for the object behind a validation, a copy over the plate's edge, an object out of a nozzle's reach and a slicing step warning. Holds no rule about what a problem is. |
| `issues_from` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue` | The rule, as plain data with its own tests: an object lookup's entry exists only while OrcaSlicer holds a notification of its kind; a print-problem notification no lookup answers for is a plate-wide issue in OrcaSlicer's words. |
| `PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout`, `IssueOverlay` | Where the pieces go and how they are drawn, with ImGui inside the canvas's frame through the same overlay hook as the tool strip. The bubble never covers its object, the pill, the open list, a confirmation or the tool strip. |
| `PrintIssues/IssueContext`, `AgentHost::submit_issue_message` | The chat message a button sends, and the one way a message enters the chat from outside the page. |

Two things are read whether or not a notification exists, because OrcaSlicer's notifications do not cover them in time:

- **The slice result.** A path outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach, and a filament that cannot print on the plate surface get their notifications only when OrcaSlicer's preview loads the slice, which here means opening Check print. OrcaSlicer refuses to print from the moment the slice ends.
- **Why a slice failed.** A critical failure is shown in a dialog and leaves no notification, and no notification says which object the failure named. `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` is the only place both exist.

Rules that follow:

- **Never "no issues" before a check.** While OrcaSlicer holds an unapplied edit the status says it is checking and both buttons are off.
- **Nothing is resolved by the fork.** An issue goes when OrcaSlicer lets go of its notification. An agent saying it fixed something changes nothing.
- **"Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's answer.** An error-level notification blocks. For the slice result it is OrcaSlicer's own post-slice check, which allows a path 2 mm past the plate edge; the monitor does not apply a stricter test of its own.
- **The object is never read out of the words.** Two messages of one kind are told apart by comparing OrcaSlicer's words now with its words before, as OrcaSlicer does itself. Which object a message is about always comes from a check's own ids.
- **A press acts on what is true at the press**, and with no assistant set up it sends nothing and offers the chat panel's setup. **Ask AI may only read.**
- **Operation failures are not print issues.** A failed download or a refused arrange is a confirmation, never an entry in the issue list.

Known limits: application and account notifications (update available, plug-in missing, preset sync conflict) are routed to `App` and drawn nowhere yet. A confirmation shows OrcaSlicer's words and a close button; the actions OrcaSlicer attached to its own notification (open folder, eject, cancel an upload) are not offered. Work that is running is shown as words, without a bar. The tips and the object size card are not shown.

'''

open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
p=r+'orca-integration-guide.md'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
a=s[s.index("### Print problems are read back from OrcaSlicer, not recorded as they pass\n"):s.index("### Application teardown can re-enter destroyed owners\n")]
b='''### OrcaSlicer's notifications are read back, not drawn

OrcaSlicer reports print problems through three unrelated producers (print
validation in `Plater`, slicing steps on the background thread, plate checks in
`GLCanvas3D`), and results of actions from dozens of call sites. All of them
end in `NotificationManager`. Inside the shell that list is the source of
truth for what JusPrin draws (see "Print issues and OrcaSlicer's
notifications" in the architecture guide). What was learned about it:

- **Three additions to `NotificationManager`, 13 lines in all.**
  `for_each_notification` visits the type, level and current text of every
  notification that is shown. `update_notifications` calls
  `report_notifications_updated()` on its first line. `render_notifications`
  skips its drawing loop while the Prepare canvas has its legacy overlays
  hidden.
- **The observer call is first in `update_notifications`, not last.** That
  function returns early while the application window is not the active one.
  With the call after that return, nothing would be read while the person
  types to an agent in another application. It runs on every idle turn of
  every canvas, so the listener only compares, and rebuilds on a change
  (343 comparisons to 11 rebuilds in one test run).
- **Only the drawing loop is skipped, never the end of
  `render_notifications`.** The end deletes a closed plate warning and records
  the time of the draw. `PlaterWarningNotification::close()` only hides the
  notification and relies on that deletion; a hidden one makes OrcaSlicer
  refuse to push the same words again. An early return from the function left
  such warnings stuck for the session. It asks the Prepare canvas rather than
  the canvas being drawn: Check print is a second canvas whose own flag is
  never set.
- **Hidden means absent.** The accessor leaves out a hidden notification, as
  `get_notification_count()` does. OrcaSlicer hides validation and plate
  warnings while its preview is shown.
- **A notification has no readable target.** The object is captured inside the
  "Jump to" callback. So the object comes from asking the check again:
  `Print::validate` (public, `const`, under a millisecond on small plates, one
  error and one warning at most), `ModelInstance::print_volume_state`,
  `GLCanvas3D::check_volumes_outside_state` with its `ObjectFilamentResults`,
  and `step_state_with_warnings`. A warning's `type` is left uninitialised by
  some producers, so never use it for identity.
- **Slice-result problems are notified late.** `_set_warning_notification_if_needed`
  runs when the preview canvas loads the G-code. Right after a slice the list
  holds none of: path outside the plate, nozzle reach, plate surface. They are
  in `PartPlate::get_slice_result()` at once, and
  `is_slice_result_ready_for_print()` already refuses.
- **A critical slicing failure leaves no notification.** `Plater` shows a
  dialog instead. `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED`, which `Plater.cpp` defines and no
  header declares, carries the reason and the object;
  `Workspace/PlaterProjectState.hpp` declares it, and `Plater.cpp` includes
  that header ahead of the definition, so no OrcaSlicer line changes. The
  handler bound later runs first and must `Skip()`.
- **The print lags the project by up to 500 ms.**
  `Plater::is_background_process_update_scheduled()` is true until OrcaSlicer
  applies an edit; until then neither the print nor the notifications describe
  the project as it is. This is what separates "checking" from "no issues".
- **A closed notification returns only with the next real edit.** OrcaSlicer
  validates again when applying an edit changes the print, not when an update
  is merely scheduled.
- **Some plate checks are quieter than they look.** `check_tpu_printable_status`
  returns true unconditionally. The PLA with PETG warning is skipped when the
  printer has a tool change time above zero, which the Bambu Lab H2D profile
  does. A brim is trimmed at the plate edge and at a nozzle's reach; a skirt is
  what puts a path outside.
- **OrcaSlicer validates only the active plate.**

'''
s=s.replace(a,b)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
EOF

The redesign is built and passes every test I have, in my worktree on top of the print-issues commit `6394191523`. Nothing is committed.

## The rule you asked me to check

Covered at the start of this turn: the original rule is "do not parse translated prose for identity" (first handoff, line 54), with no other reason given, so comparing OrcaSlicer's live text with its earlier live text is fine and I went ahead. Which object a message is about still never comes from its words.

## What now works

- **OrcaSlicer's message list decides what JusPrin shows.** A table routes all 62 message kinds. If OrcaSlicer adds a kind, the build stops until someone routes it.
- **Print problems** appear in the issue list as before, with the bubble and highlight. The flushing-volume warning is now there too.
- **"Export finished" and similar** appear as a short confirmation above the pill, with a close button. The screenshot I sent shows it.
- **Three of the four bugs are fixed:** the wrong "blocks printing" label, warnings stuck after switching to the classic view, and the missing object on "nozzle can't reach". The "Filaments 1" wording is left alone, as I recommended.

## Two places I departed from what we said

1. **The "look again" line is first in OrcaSlicer's function, not last.** That function exits early when JusPrin is not the front window. At the end, the list would freeze while you talk to an agent in another app. One of my runs had the window in the background the whole time and passed.
2. **I deleted the code that rebuilt the filament and nozzle warning sentences.** Those warnings point at no object, so OrcaSlicer's own message is shown as is.

One finding changed point 3 of the design slightly: a serious slicing failure shows a dialog and leaves nothing in OrcaSlicer's list. So the failed-slice reason comes from the "slice finished" signal on its own, like the slice-result readers.

## Test results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| The feature's own 42-step run in the real app (one step changed, one added) | 43 steps, 361 checks, 0 failed |
| My reproductions (two nozzles, mixed materials, slicing cases) | 33 steps, 212 checks, 0 failed |
| General app run | 526 checks, 0 failed |
| Switch to classic view | 31 checks, 0 failed |
| Unit tests | all pass |

OrcaSlicer's code changes by 13 added lines and 2 replaced, in two files. That set merges into today's OrcaSlicer with no new conflicts.

## Not done

- **Buttons on confirmations.** There is no "Open folder", "Eject" or "Cancel upload" yet, only close.
- **Progress** shows as words, with no bar.
- **Update and account messages** are routed but shown nowhere; they need a place on Home.
- **Dark mode, Windows and Linux** are untested.
- **Current `jusprin-newui`.** It has moved on since the feature was taken off it, and this work is not rebased onto it.

## Your call

1. Do you want this committed? If so, I'd commit onto `feature-popup-message-handling`, unless you want a different branch.
2. Should I rebase it onto current `jusprin-newui` next, or leave it on the feature branch until you've looked?

The report is updated at `investigation-print-issues-four-gaps.md` in my worktree. The whole change is also saved as one patch in `investigation-print-issues-four-gaps/redesign/redesign.patch`.

content.text:
Two answers: the not-shown list, then progress bars.

## Which messages are not shown

It was identifiable from the code but not easy: one table of 62 rows, where you had to know that a certain label meant "drawn nowhere". So I regrouped that table in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/NoticeKinds.cpp` into five lists, each under a comment saying what happens to those messages:

- **Print problems (19):** go to the issue list.
- **Outcomes of an action (19):** drawn as a confirmation. The comment says what is missing: the buttons OrcaSlicer attached, such as "open folder" and "eject".
- **Running work (6):** drawn as words. The comment says the bar and cancel are missing.
- **NOT SHOWN ANYWHERE YET (15):** update, plug-in and account messages, each with a one-line note on what it is.
- **NOT SHOWN, on purpose (3):** slicing progress (the header has it), the startup tips, and the object size card.

The list cannot go stale, because the build fails unless every OrcaSlicer message kind is in exactly one of the five. It behaves the same as before; the kind tests pass (204 assertions). I did not rebuild the app itself, so your running test session is untouched.

## Progress bars

No, and one of your two is not a message at all.

**STL import is not a message.** It uses a separate pop-up window with its own bar ("Loading…"). Nothing in this work touches it, so it still shows.

**Four kinds of message draw a progress bar:**

| Message | When it appears | Buttons beside the bar | In JusPrin now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slicing progress | Slicing, and exporting right after | Cancel | Shown in the header, with cancel |
| Background job | Arrange, auto-orient, fill the plate, text and SVG tools, lay-on-face in the rotate tool, SLA import | Cancel | Words only if the job reports a status; no bar, no cancel |
| Upload to a network printer | Sending a file to a Klipper or OctoPrint style printer | Cancel; error state | Words only |
| Download from a link | Opening a model link from a website | Pause, cancel, open | Words only |

Sending to a Bambu printer, binding a printer and plug-in downloads also have bars, but inside their own dialog windows, so they are unaffected too.

The background-job row is from reading the code; I have not watched an arrange in the running app to see what words appear, if any. Arrange on a small plate finishes too fast to matter, but on a full plate the missing cancel would be felt.

If you want bars, the header beside slicing progress is the natural place. One decision is yours first: whether upload progress should come from the message, or from the upload queue's own signals, which also carry cancel and errors.

How complicated is it to show these messages and their progress inside the chat panel? When the agent is not set up, we just s show it right above the "setup agent" block. If it's setup, we make it a dynamic UI element at the current timeline with a themam cancel button and the status updates when the The progress is done or cancelled.

Moderately complicated, and most of the pieces already exist. The work is mainly in the chat page. One product hole needs deciding first: the chat panel can be closed.

## What already exists

- **A progress bar and a card with a cancel button in the chat timeline.** The chat page draws these today for the agent's own tool calls (for example when the agent starts a slice).
- **A way for the app to push rows into the timeline that no chat message caused.** External tools connected to JusPrin already get cards this way.
- **The "set up agent" screens**, where a slot above them is page-only work.

## What has to be built

1. **App side: one feed of "work in progress".** It gathers the four sources, each with a title, a state (running, done, cancelled, failed), a percentage if known, and whether it can be cancelled.
2. **Two new messages between app and page:** "here is the current work" and "cancel this one". These are additive, so older pages are unaffected.
3. **Page side: one card**, built from the existing bar and button, placed at the current point in the timeline, or above the setup block when no agent is set up. It needs a design pass for its states.
4. **Remove the words-only version from the 3D view**, so progress is not shown twice.

## Where each source stands

| Source | Percentage | Cancel | Extra OrcaSlicer lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slicing | Available | Available (the header uses it) | None |
| Upload to a network printer | Available from the upload queue's own signals | Available | None |
| Background jobs (arrange, orient, fill plate, text tools) | Not reachable today | Available | One to three more lines for a real bar; otherwise a bar with no percentage |
| Download from a link | Signals exist | Not checked | Not checked |

## Things you should decide

1. **Chat panel closed.** Progress inside a closed panel is invisible. Options: open the panel when work starts, keep a small fallback on the 3D view, or accept it. Slicing is not affected, since the header has it.
2. **Slicing.** Does it stay in the header only, or also appear in the chat?
3. **After it finishes.** Does the card stay in the timeline as a one-line record, and is that record saved with the project? I'd keep it for the session and not save it.
4. **During a reply.** If the agent is mid-reply, does the card go above or below the reply being written? I have not looked at how the page orders these.

## Size

Roughly the size of the redesign I just built, with the larger half in the chat page and its tests. The app side is small, because three of the four sources already publish what is needed.

content.text:
Progress messages in the chat are built and pass their unit tests, but I have not yet run them in the real app. That last step needs the test app you have open to be closed, because rebuilding replaces the program it is running from.

## What is built

- **A saved work record.** Each slice, arrange or export is saved with the project at the point in the chat where it started. A message that arrives later appears below it.
- **A card in the chat.** It shows a progress bar while the work runs, a Cancel button where the work can be stopped, and "Done", "Cancelled" or the failure reason when it ends.
- **The panel opens when work starts.**
- **Slicing appears in both places,** the header and the chat.
- **Not set up yet:** the card appears at the end of the chat, directly above the setup block. No special case was needed; the setup block already sits below the timeline.
- **Running work is no longer drawn on the 3D view.** Outcomes such as "Exported successfully" still are.

## The three things I said I would handle

- A record saved mid-run reads "Interrupted when the project was closed" when the project is reopened.
- Repeats collapse in the display ("Slicing plate 1 · 3 times"). Nothing is merged in the saved file.
- Export records carry no folder path; an upload record does carry the printer's address (see below).

## Tested so far

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Chat host tests (4 new cases: placement, progress, cancel, interruption, saving) | 4,791 assertions pass |
| Chat page tests (8 new) | 409 pass, type check clean |
| Real-app steps: slice, cancel a slice, failed slice, arrange | Written and compiling; **not run** |

## What you should know

- **Slicing has a real percentage and a known ending.** Everything else (arrange, export, upload, download) shows a bar with no percentage, and its ending is recorded as "Done" unless you pressed Cancel. OrcaSlicer's message for those says only that the work is running.
- **Arrange may show two cards.** OrcaSlicer raises two "running" messages for it. I'll see which on the first real run and merge them if so.
- **Upload records include the printer's address,** because they use OrcaSlicer's own line. Say if you want that stripped.
- **Upload and download are untested** and will stay so here: there is no network printer or download link in the test setup.

## What I need

Quit the test app (Cmd+Q) when you are done with it, and tell me. I'll then rebuild, run the real-app steps, fix what they show, and relaunch it for you with the progress cards in.

Make OrcaSlicer's notification list the source of truth, and show running work in the chat

Inside the JusPrin shell OrcaSlicer's own notifications are held but not

else. That left four gaps: the outcome of an action (export finished, an
arrange that was refused) was shown nowhere, the "flushing volume set to 0"
warning was missing, a warning kind OrcaSlicer adds later would be invisible,
and most of the readers had never been triggered.

Now the notification list decides what exists, and JusPrin draws what it
holds.

Print issues. PrintIssues/NoticeKinds routes each of OrcaSlicer's 62
notification kinds: print problem, outcome of an action, running work,
application state, or not shown. Every kind is named in one of five lists,
and a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in that file until someone routes
it. A print-problem notification becomes an issue in OrcaSlicer's words. A
notification carries no object, so where OrcaSlicer lets its check be asked
again (validation, a copy over the plate's edge, an object out of a nozzle's
reach, a slicing step warning) the check is asked once more for the object
only, and that entry exists only while OrcaSlicer holds a notification of
its kind. The rule is issues_from in PrintIssues/PrintIssue, plain data with
its own tests. The plate-check readers that composed OrcaSlicer's sentences
are gone: those warnings name no object, so the notification is shown as it
is.

Two things are still read whether or not a notification exists. The slice
result: a path outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach and a
filament that cannot print on the plate surface get their notifications only
when Check print loads the slice, while OrcaSlicer refuses to print from the
moment the slice ends. And why a slice failed: a critical failure shows a
dialog and leaves no notification.

The monitor is told to look again on the first line of
NotificationManager::update_notifications, compares cheaply, and rebuilds
only on a change. Four of its five signals are gone; the slice-finished
event stays, as the only place a failed slice's object exists.

Outcomes. The outcome of an action is drawn as a short confirmation above
the status pill, in OrcaSlicer's words, with a close button that closes
OrcaSlicer's own notification.

Running work. A slice, an arrange and an export are shown in the chat, not
on the canvas (PrintIssues/WorkFeed, AgentHost::begin_work, update_work,

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Show OrcaSlicer's notifications in JusPrin's own way: print issues, confirmations, and work in the chat

Inside the JusPrin shell OrcaSlicer's own pop-up notifications are held but
no longer drawn. JusPrin reads the list back and draws what it holds:

- Print problems: a status in the lower right corner of the Prepare canvas,
  the list it opens, and a bubble beside the object the selected issue is
  about, with Ask AI and Resolve with AI.
- The outcome of an action (export finished, an arrange that was refused): a
  short confirmation above the status, with a close button that closes
  OrcaSlicer's own notification.
- Work that is still running (a slice, an arrange, an export): an entry in
  the chat with a progress bar and, where the work can be stopped, Cancel.

This is two commits from feature-popup-message-handling as one: the first
print-issues design (6394191523), which was taken off this branch for a
rethink, and the redesign that followed (0c3bbcce42).

OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth. PrintIssues/NoticeKinds
routes each of its 62 notification kinds: print problem, outcome of an
action, running work, application state, or not shown. Every kind is named
in one of five lists, and a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in that
file until someone routes it. A print-problem notification becomes an issue
in OrcaSlicer's words. A notification carries no object, so where OrcaSlicer
lets its check be asked again (validation, a copy over the plate's edge, an
object out of a nozzle's reach, a slicing step warning) the check is asked
once more for the object only, and that entry exists only while OrcaSlicer
holds a notification of its kind. The rule is issues_from in
PrintIssues/PrintIssue, plain data with its own tests. Nothing here decides
whether something is a problem.

Two things are read whether or not a notification exists. The slice result:
a path outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach and a filament
that cannot print on the plate surface get their notifications only when
Check print loads the slice, while OrcaSlicer refuses to print from the
moment the slice ends. And why a slice failed: a critical failure shows a
dialog and leaves no notification. It is read from EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED,
which Plater.cpp defines and no header declared; a fork header Plater.cpp
already includes declares it, with no OrcaSlicer line changed.

PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor is told to look again on the first line of
NotificationManager::update_notifications, compares cheaply, and rebuilds
only on a change. While OrcaSlicer holds an edit it has not yet applied to
the print, the issues are marked stale, the status says it is checking, and
the buttons are off, so "no print issues" is never shown before a check.
Only the active plate is reported, because that is the only plate OrcaSlicer
checks. "Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's own answer, never a stricter test
of the fork's.

Canvas (PrintIssues/IssueOverlay, IssueOverlayLayout): drawn with ImGui
through the overlay hook the tool strip uses. The bubble goes above its
object, else right, left or below, and never covers the object, the status,
the open list, a confirmation or the tool strip. It docks beside the status
for a plate-wide issue or an object out of view. Every finding on one object
shares the bubble through a pager. Selecting an issue selects its copy by
OrcaSlicer's own id.

Chat (AgentHost::submit_issue_message, PrintIssues/IssueContext): a press on
Ask AI or Resolve with AI becomes an ordinary user message, the request
sentence with OrcaSlicer's words quoted beneath it, and carries the issue,
its target and the freshness of the evidence as data for the model. The
issue is looked up again at the press, so one that has cleared or gone stale
is not sent. Ask AI may only read: the turn is offered the read-only tools
and the host refuses a call to any other. With no assistant set up, a press
sends nothing and offers to open the chat panel's setup.

Running work (PrintIssues/WorkFeed, AgentHost::begin_work, update_work,
finish_work, WorkCard in the page): an entry is saved with the project at
the place in the timeline where the work started, so a message that arrives
later reads below it, and it is completed in place. The chat panel opens
when work starts. Slicing is also still in the header. A slice is followed
through OrcaSlicer's own events, which carry a percentage and an outcome;
other work is read from the "still running" notifications, which carry
neither. The page folds repeats into one line with a count; nothing is
merged in what is saved. An entry still "running" in a project that was
closed mid-run reads as interrupted. Bridge: two additive messages,
work_updated and work_cancel, behind the capability work_log.

OrcaSlicer-owned files: NotificationManager.cpp and .hpp, 13 added lines.
for_each_notification visits the type, level and text of every notification
that is shown. update_notifications calls the fork's observer first, before
its early return for an inactive window, so the list is still read while the
person works in another application. render_notifications skips its drawing
loop while the Prepare canvas has its legacy overlays hidden, the flag the
shell already sets on install and restores when switching to the classic
view. Only the loop is skipped: the end of that function deletes a closed
plate warning, and skipping it left such warnings hidden for the session.
The Prepare canvas is asked, not the canvas being drawn, because Check print
is a second canvas without the flag. No upstream line is deleted or
rewritten.

Rebase evidence for those 13 lines (fork base 3ffb9585d2, upstream/main
3ca182a98e, git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base, measured on
0c3bbcce42): 3,892 conflicted files with and without them, the same list,
and the one conflict block in NotificationManager.cpp predates this work.

The shell harness gains --print-issues (the lifecycle: validation,
placement, slicing warnings and failures, camera and object moves, both
buttons, stale and cleared issues, deletion, undo, plate switch, project
replacement, Check print), --print-issue-readers (what the one-nozzle test
printer cannot reach: two nozzles, mixed materials, paths outside the plate,
a failed slice naming its object, a result confirmed on the canvas, and the
work log), and --manual-print-issues for hands-on use.

Known limits, recorded in agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md and beside the
kind table: application and account notifications (update available,
plug-in missing, preset sync conflict) are routed and drawn nowhere yet; a
confirmation does not offer the action OrcaSlicer attached to its
notification (open folder, eject); only a slice has a percentage and a known
ending; uploads and downloads have not been run. Not run in dark mode, on
Windows or on Linux.
EOF
